summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare triggered by a high-fat meal, presenting with severe abdominal pain and nausea. She was managed with IV fluids, bowel rest, and IV hydromorphone, later transitioned to oral Dilaudid. TPN was restarted for nutritional support and malnutrition. She developed a brief fever without infection source; imaging showed a right lower lobe consolidation likely due to prior aspiration, but no antibiotics were needed. Platelet count decreased slightly with no clear cause, and heparin flushes were discontinued. Constipation was managed with a bowel regimen. Pain and symptoms improved, and she was discharged home on oral pain medication, anti-nausea drugs, bowel regimen, and continued TPN with plans for weekly monitoring.
